summary.text: Aidan McLindon, a City of Whittlesea councillor for Kirrip Ward, is standing as an independent for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election. He represented Beaudesert in the Queensland Parliament from 2009 to 2012, elected for the Liberal National Party before leaving it to found The Queensland Party, which he later merged into Katter's Australian Party. In Victoria he contested Mulgrave in 2022 as deputy leader of the Freedom Party, and Werribee at its 2025 by-election. He became Whittlesea's mayor in November 2024, was suspended from the council for six months in April 2025 and came back as a councillor that October.
summary.note: No source names the Mill Park candidate as the former Queensland MP and Whittlesea councillor of the same name; the match rests on the uncommon name and Mill Park being in the City of Whittlesea.

legal_and_integrity.text: Suspended from the City of Whittlesea council for six months from April 2025, after councillors passed a no-confidence motion in him as mayor, on the ground that his behaviour endangered councillors' and staff members' health and safety; he denied the claims of intimidating conduct. A Commission of Inquiry set up by the state government reported in October 2025 that his performance as mayor had fallen short in many respects.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: He served the suspension and returned to the council in October 2025, no longer as mayor, and the state government put monitors back into the council for the rest of 2025.

summary.text: Arthur Tsoutsoulis is One Nation's candidate for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election. He has worked for over two decades in traffic and transport engineering and in managing civil projects. He stood for One Nation in the federal seat of Scullin in 2025, where the ABC puts his first-preference share at 6.6 per cent.

priorities.text: Open government, including transparency on funding and debt
Safer roads and renewed road infrastructure
Community safety, local businesses and local jobs
Help with living costs, affordable housing and action on homelessness
Ending repeated state taxes on assets people already own

summary.text: Binoy Zacharias is the Greens candidate for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he is a self-employed mortgage broker who earlier worked as a library technician, and he says Mill Park has been his home for 18 years. On his party page he describes himself as a parent, carer and disability rights advocate, and names public transport, green spaces and housing affordability as local gaps.

priorities.text: a positive voice for putting people’s interests over company profits
Affordable and frequent public transport for the area
Better protection of parks and green spaces
Housing affordability
Disability rights, and services that respect everyone's dignity

summary.text: Elizabeth Nealy is Labor's candidate for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election, a seat left open by the retirement of Lily D'Ambrosio. She has taught in Melbourne's northern suburbs for about two decades. She represented Beale Ward on Banyule City Council from 2020 until resigning in July 2026, serving two one-year terms as mayor, and was a Whittlesea councillor from 2005 to 2008.

prior_roles.note: The ABC says she was mayor for two one-year terms and gives the years of the later one only.

priorities.text: Health, cost of living and the state school system
Local facilities and infrastructure, as she pursued on council

summary.text: Eve Levens is the Animal Justice Party's candidate for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election. She works as a clerk in local hospitals, holds degrees in psychology and applied linguistics, and has lived locally for about 12 years. Her party page says she has spoken at council forums on pet desexing, impounded animals and wildlife, and names mental health and housing as other concerns.

priorities.text: Stronger enforcement of animal welfare laws and less exploitation of animals
Greater protection for wildlife
Free desexing and microchipping of pets, and no killing of impounded animals
Responding to mental illness with compassion and less stigma
Housing affordability and security

summary.text: Jesse Lambourn is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election. Lambourn teaches at a public school, belongs to the Australian Education Union and has campaigned through the party's Socialists in Schools group. The campaign page argues that Victoria's public schools are underfunded and opposes a proposed AI data centre in South Morang.

priorities.text: put working-class people and our communities before corporate interests
Full funding for public schools and other public services
Relief from the cost of groceries, rent and mortgages
Opposing the proposed South Morang AI data centre in favour of housing, green space and infrastructure

summary.text: Joel Drysdale is the Liberal candidate for Mill Park at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in regional Victoria, moved to Melbourne at 21, and owns a small business as a publican and brewer; his party page says he lives in Epping. He was earlier the Liberal candidate for the federal seat of Scullin but withdrew in March 2025.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists him as withdrawing in March 2025 over section 44 concerns.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of living
Support for small businesses and less red tape
Restoring community safety
